title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 227 (Legal advisers and bankers not to disclose certain information)

content.overview: Section 227 provides that nothing in this Chapter shall require the disclosure by a legal adviser of any privileged communication made to him in that capacity, except as respects the name and address of his client, or by a banker of any information as to the affairs of any of his customers other than the company or other body corporate under investigation. The privilege is limited: it does not allow withholding of the company’s own records, and it is not a general right of silence for company officers.
content.glance: Legal adviser need not disclose privileged communications (except client name and address); banker need not disclose affairs of customers other than the company under investigation; limited privilege — not a shield for company officers or company records.
content.study: Nothing in this Chapter shall require the disclosure to the Tribunal or to the Central Government or to the Registrar or to an inspector appointed by the Central Government—(a) by a legal adviser, of any privileged communication made to him in that capacity, except as respects the name and address of his client; or (b) by a banker of any company or other body corporate, of any information as to the affairs of any of his customers other than such company or body corporate. Current-law framing: identify the claimant of privilege (legal adviser or banker); apply the limited exceptions (client name/address; company under investigation is not protected as a ‘other customer’); reject any attempt to use the section as a general officers’ silence right or to withhold the company’s own books.

sections.heading: Legal Adviser
sections.body: Need not disclose privileged communications made to him in that capacity, except the name and address of the client.

sections.heading: Banker
sections.body: Need not disclose information as to the affairs of any customer other than the company or body corporate under investigation.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body: Does not protect the company’s own records; not a general right of silence for officers; privilege is limited to the professional confidence stated.

provisions.title: Legal advisers and bankers not to disclose certain information

examples.title: Privileged legal advice
examples.body: An inspector demands that the company’s external counsel disclose the content of legal advice given to the board. Under s. 227 the legal adviser need not disclose that privileged communication, except the client’s name and address.

examples.title: Banker’s other customers
examples.body: The company’s bank is asked for details of another customer’s accounts unconnected with the company under investigation. Section 227 does not require the banker to disclose those other customers’ affairs.

hypotheticals.question: May a director refuse to answer the inspector by citing s. 227 privilege?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 227 protects legal advisers’ privileged communications and bankers’ other customers. It is not a general right of silence for company officers. Officers remain under the duties and powers in ss. 217 and related provisions.

distinctions.title: Privilege for legal advisers/bankers (s. 227) vs powers of inspectors (s. 217)
distinctions.left: Limited non-disclosure for legal advisers and bankers
distinctions.right: Inspector’s civil-court powers and duty of officers to assist

misconceptions.trap: Section 227 allows any officer to refuse to produce company books by claiming privilege.
misconceptions.correction: Section 227 is limited to legal advisers’ privileged communications (except client name/address) and bankers’ information about other customers. It does not authorise withholding of the company’s own records or a general officers’ silence.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 227 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify claimant (legal adviser / banker). II. Apply limited privilege. III. Exclude company records and officers’ general silence. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Role of claimant; nature of communication; privilege scope; precise relief.

examTips: Banker: other customers only — not the company under investigation.
